That's an incredibly optimistic view of gameplay. If your armor is breaking after hundreds of points of damage, it's because you've spent an extended time in a less-than-optimal situation. It's because there's a group of enemies flanking your cover, or you're having to stand in the open and fix a tool *again*, or because you ran around a corner into a heavily armored foe.

In such situations, you're going to take additional damage past the armor threshold. You're going to take attrition damage, because nobody has the reflexes *and* opportunity to take cover against all threats every single time their armor breaks. Depending on the stress level, this attrition is going to be 5% or 50% of your health - and regaining that loss is essential for long-term objective camping (i.e. half of the game's loud objectives).

I don't know how long you've been playing this game, but prior to health regeneration being a thing (the introduction of a specific character and their unique abilities), the hardest missions were the marathon missions - certain notable ones were recognized for requiring tight resource management and even tactical use of arrests and trades in order to survive the grueling slog-fest. Now anyone can stand and fight indefinitely, with equipment used to cover mistakes, difficult enemy spawns, and other unexpected losses.

**tl;dr:** A build without health regeneration is a build that's going to eventually need medical supplies to survive, and that puts an upper limit on how long you can perform well. Don't be foolish, include health regeneration in your build and turn your health into more armor.

Right, let's break down your post bit by bit.

> **Skills that used to be top tier are now unlocked at the very beginning**

These skills are endurance, stealth basics, burglary skills, domination basics, and feedback skills. That's two advanced skills, two basic skills, and a high-level skill of questionable usefulness. While you're technically correct in that a "top tier" skill is now available for everyone, it's feedback. How often does anyone use it?

> **you can max out like 3 trees at once**

You can max out a little over two and a half sub-trees at once. Ignoring the initial equipment unlock, which is now free for everyone, there's still 18 skills in each of the five skill trees. Maxing out a sub-tree is just like buying a third of an old skill tree, except now you don't need to waste points on filler to reach the highest tier and can just go straight for what you need.

> **anybody can use any deployable regardless of build**

Most aggressive builds could bring medical supplies, ammunition, feedback devices, and first aid kits anyway because we were all buying mandatory skills in various roles. Stealth builds don't need any of those, and were bringing feedback devices or body bags anyway because of the stealth skills in their respective trees.

> **there's like 3 perk decks that let you constantly gain health back**

All regeneration decks were present before the major update. Only one deck has constant regeneration. Its regeneration rate was nerfed during the update.

> **the sentry guns. Oh god, the sentry guns.**

This is a valid concern. Most of us do see the need for a sentry gun nerf, and there's been discussions about the best way to do it.

> **When I'm creating my skill builds, I no longer feel like I'm specializing myself. When you unlock new skills and tiers, it no longer feels like you're slowly improving as a specific role. Instead, it feels like you just went up into a dream state and you're picking out what superpowers you want.**

Build meta is now flatter and blurrier. There's no such thing as rigidly-defined roles anymore. Nobody can point to half a dozen skills and say "you must take these". There's a lot more options available, but you can't take more of them.

> **I've been using a regeneration deck along with a hybrid build, and with a shotgun I can regenerate almost all my health in less than a minute. On a high difficulty.**

Welcome to the new build meta. There's fewer wrong choices, and you can play how you want instead of what's best. Did you have fun? If you enjoyed yourself, then it's a success.

> **There used to be one skill that made your drills go faster, one skill that sometimes gave your drills an autofix, and another that made your drills quieter. Now, that's all one skill. At the very start of the skill tree.**

> [...]

>  **Now, imagine leveling up for the first time now. Congratulations, you put your first skill point into technician! Remember that old drill? Well, now it's almost completely upgraded right from the get-go!**

The basic drill speed skill still costs the same. The autofix skill used to cost 3 points. Now it's split into two skills, and requires a total of 9 points to purchase. The drilling speed skill used to be 4 points, now it costs 6 points. Drill skills are _more expensive_ to purchase now. The only exception is the silent drilling skill, which is now free - but it's always been next to useless and a total waste of points (even on stealth, where silent tools are superior).

Medical bags are primarily about resupplying downs instead of health. None of the decks will let you survive being caught in the open in front of a dozen enemies and a stun unit, but medical bags will let you recover from it once you're picked back up. For the gaming community, 80-damage rifles are referred to as Battle Rifles to differentiate them from 40-damage Assault Rifles and 120+ damage Designated Marksman Rifles (DMRs). All three categories have different handling and roles.

We use the term "DMR" because the release of DMR Kits allowed us to modify Assault Rifles and Battle Rifles into pseudo-sniper rifles. One specific model was renamed to fit with its new counterparts.

We use the term "Battle Rifle" because the real-world counterparts of certain 80-damage rifles use full-size rifle cartridges and qualify for the real-world "battle rifle" designation.
